Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas · Conversation, family & daily routines

behaviour noun

the way someone acts

also behavior, conduct, good behaviour, bad behaviour, ways

classical

Cic. Off. 1.90: quantō superiōrēs sīmus, tantō nōs gerāmus summissius
Cic. Fam. 11.27.5: quōnam modō gererem mē adversus Caesarem

sē gerere

phrase: gerō with the reflexive, and an adverb or a clause of manner

behave, conduct oneself (well, badly, modestly …)

Latin says how someone behaved with a verb and an adverb where English uses the noun: optimē sē gessit, his behaviour was excellent. Lewis & Short: “to bear, deport, behave, or conduct one’s self”.

Other words

  • mōrēs, mōrum m. pl. — behaviour, ways, manners; character

    noun, second declension, plural · also used · classical · Plin. Ep. 3.3.7: ā quō mōrēs prīmum mox ēloquentiam discat; Hor. Ars 156: aetātis cujusque notandī sunt tibi mōrēs

    The plural of mōs, custom (see practice): a person’s habitual behaviour and character, good or bad. Lewis & Short: “conduct, behavior; in plur., manners, morals, character”.

Examples

  • rēctē praecipere videantur, quī monent, ut, quantō superiōrēs sīmus, tantō nōs gerāmus summissius

    those seem to give good advice who warn us that the higher we stand, the more humbly we should behaveCic. Off. 1.90

  • ā quō mōrēs prīmum mox ēloquentiam discat, quae male sine mōribus discitur

    from whom he may learn good conduct first, then eloquence, which is badly learned without itPlin. Ep. 3.3.7

  • in maximīs rēbus quōnam modō gererem mē adversus Caesarem, ūsus tuō cōnsiliō sum

    in matters of the greatest moment I took your advice on how I should behave towards CaesarCic. Fam. 11.27.5

See also behave, well-behaved, practice.
